validity.researcher_notes: The branch is real and still planned. A 2020 FederalPress article gives 277 km. The recorded start year of 2023 has passed. The newest source on this branch, a November 2023 news item, moves gas to Slavgorod to 2027, and a 2025 item on the Rubtsovsk branch shows further delay, so 2027 is probably too early too. No citation gives a firm new date. The capacity of 0.86 is cited to a government order whose readable text does not name this branch, so it is not confirmed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The newest source naming this branch is a November 2023 news item that moves gas to Slavgorod to 2027. A 2025 item on the sister Rubtsovsk branch shows the program still running with later dates. Dormancy rule checked: nothing says this branch was dropped, so proposed stays, but no source after 2023 names the Slavgorod branch itself.

wiki_citations_read.note: Bankfax of March 1998 says the existing Novosibirsk-Barnaul pipeline, 292 km, was finished by the end of 1996. It is the older operating line, not the planned Rebrikha branches.
Interactive LNG dashboard page. It has nothing on this pipeline.
Altai government item from 2016 about the 76 km branch to Rebrikha village. It is the Rebrikha branch, not the Rubtsovsk or Slavgorod branches.
Politsib of 30 July 2020, read as a Wayback copy. Work on the Rebrikha branch restarted after a pause. It does not give figures for the Rubtsovsk or Slavgorod branches.

Altayskaya Pravda, December 2021, read as a Wayback copy. The Rebrikha branch and gas station are finished, and the page says they open the way to later gas supply for Slavgorod and Rubtsovsk. No figures for the two branches.
Contractor page for the Rebrikha branch and gas station, read as a Wayback copy. It covers the Rebrikha work only.
Rossiyskaya Gazeta of April 2021. The 2021 to 2025 agreement with Gazprom covers two trunk branches to Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod, 600 km together. It gives no figure for each branch.

FederalPress of 30 July 2020, read as a Wayback copy. Says the Rebrikha-Rubtsovsk branch will be 246 km and the Rebrikha-Slavgorod branch 277 km, fed from the Rebrikha branch and tied to the Novosibirsk-Barnaul pipeline. Supports both sheet lengths.

Gazprom release of 1 December 2020, read as a Wayback copy. The 2021 to 2025 program includes 600 km of branch pipelines to Rebrikha, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod. It gives no per-branch length or capacity.
Gazprom gasification map page for Altai Krai. The readable text does not name the Rubtsovsk or Slavgorod branches.
Government order 816-r annex. The readable text does not name the Rebrikha, Rubtsovsk, Slavgorod or Barnaul branches and has no 0.96 or 0.86 figure. It does not support the sheet capacity.
Bankfax of 18 February 2021. The Gazprom 2021 to 2025 program includes 600 km of branch pipelines to Rebrikha, Rubtsovsk and Slavgorod, with no per-branch figures.
